name: Coatl Bastion Gunnery Team
description: Graduates of the Coatl Bastion gunnery range, the Hegemony academy's proudest export. They were taught that a shell spent at long range is a shell the enemy never gets to answer.

name: COMSEC Signals Detachment
description: A COMSEC detachment on loan, or so the paperwork claims. They redact the ship's emissions as thoroughly as they redact everything else, and nobody asks what happened to the last signals officer.

name: Auxiliary Conscripts
description: Dockhands, miners and debtors pressed into the auxiliary lists. They are cheap, they are many, and they learn to crew a ship the hard way.

name: Alpha Site Survivor
description: One of the few to walk out of Project Ziggurat's black lab at Alpha Site. They won't talk about what they saw, but they handle phase coils like someone who has seen the other side.

name: Tri-Tachyon Morale Assurance Officer
description: Tri-Tachyon's Morale Assurance keeps crews at their stations long past exhaustion. Crew who object are assured, and some of them are not seen again.

name: Sindrian Fuel Company Engineers
description: Engineers from the Sindrian Fuel Company, trained on the Diktat's antimatter plant. They squeeze every last kilometre out of a fuel load and resent being asked how.

name: Gryphon Missile Crew
description: A missile crew from a League Gryphon, drilled to keep the racks full and the tubes cycling. They take a slow reload as a personal insult.

name: Olinadu Security Detachment
description: Contract officers from Olinadu, where the police is a corporation and the corporation is the law. They are very good at kicking in doors and coming home afterwards.

name: Asher Salvage Guild Crew
description: A crew from the Church's own Asher Salvage Guild. They patch a hull with prayer and spare plating, and they find something worth keeping in every wreck.

name: Converted Hangar Deck Crew
description: Deck crew from a Church carrier, where every spare bay holds another wing. They can turn a strikecraft around faster than its pilot can finish a prayer.

name: Pather Cell
description: A Pather cell that has decided this ship is the instrument of its purpose. They strip the safeties, close the distance and make no plans for the journey home.

name: Back-Alley Cyber-Surgeon
description: A cybernetics surgeon from Kanta's court, unlicensed and unbothered. Crew are more machine than human, and those who should have died wake up with new parts and an invoice.

name: Salvager Crew
description: An independent salvage outfit in the mould of Ibrahim Interstellar Transport. They know which wrecks are worth the trip and how to keep a ship flying on scraps.

name: Ko Combine Shipbreakers
description: Shipbreakers from the Ko Combine's yard. Knowing exactly how a hull comes apart also tells them how to keep this one together long enough to be hauled home.

name: Galatia Hyperspace Physics Group
description: Researchers seconded from the Galatia Academy's Hyperspace Physics Group. They tune the drive field by hand and complain about sensor noise until someone fixes it.

name: Nanoforge Seed
description: A fragment of nanoforge fabrication matrix, still trying to build whatever it was last asked for. Wired into the missile feeds, it builds missiles.

name: Synchrotron Cell
description: A scaled-down synchrotron that brews antimatter a gram at a time. Enough to top up a ship system or two, with some left over for the tanks.

name: Fullerene Spool Integration
description: Space-elevator cable spun into the ship's frame. The hull flexes where it would have broken, and the holds take far more weight.

name: Vambrace Plating
description: Armour plating recovered alongside the Onslaught Mk.I in the Abyss. It is absurdly thick, absurdly heavy and absolutely worth it.

name: Deserter Gunners
description: Former navy gunners who left their oaths and their maintenance schedules behind. They fire fast and fix nothing.

name: Gate Hauler Drive Coil
description: A drive coil pulled from a Gate Hauler, the automated ship that carried a Gate across space. It still remembers how to move something enormous very efficiently.

name: Planetkiller Resonance Circuit
description: Engineers have managed to reverse engineer a resonance circuit salvaged from a planetkiller. Pointed at anything smaller than a world, it finds the largest thing in range and tries to shake it apart.

name: Kanta's Den Scrapdogs
description: Pirates from Kanta's Den who have never flown a ship that wasn't falling apart. Every breach is a door they know how to walk through, and every burned-out safety is one less thing slowing them down.

name: Fafnir Osmium Shell Stock
description: Crates of osmium-cored shells meant for the Navarchy's Fafnir guns, bought from a quartermaster who stopped asking where they were going. The crew hand-loads them into anything with a fixed barrel.

name: Black Hawk Breech Refit
description: Breech assemblies from a Black Hawk's refit stock, built to cram Navarchy ballistics into mounts never meant for them. The crew bolts them over the energy couplings and stops worrying about the capacitors.

name: Low Arc Shield Emitter Core
description: The emitter core of a Navarchy warship, tuned to throw a narrow shield that never moves. The crew wired it in knowing the arc would never widen, and that whatever struck it would bleed away all the faster.

name: Project Aria Retrofit
description: Conversion kits left over from Project Aria, Nightcross's long and costly weapons programme. The crew pulls the old ballistic feeds and lays energy conduit in their place, following schematics that still carry test-range stamps.

name: Ion Discharge Coils
description: Discharge coils from a crate of Nightcross ion bolters, rewound by the crew to sit behind the ship's lightest energy mounts. Whatever those guns fire now leaves as a crackling ion charge.

name: Hardlight Veil Projectors
description: Hardlight projectors pulled from a Nightcross hull, made to lace the shield with a thin veil that takes the force of each hit before it can settle in the emitters.

name: Extended Warranty Contract
description: A Nightcross extended warranty, signed in triplicate by a captain who did not read it. It covers one installed system twice over, faults included, and the monthly fees arrive with remarkable reliability.

name: Corrosion Lens Filter
description: A lens filter cut to the pattern of the Stargazer's corrosion beams. Fitted over the ship's energy turrets, it turns their light into something that eats through plating.

name: Cosmic Shunt Array
description: A shunt array that spills shield strain into the stardust between ships, where the nearest ally's grid catches it. Nobody aboard can explain how it works, only that it does.

name: Old Guard Gun Captains
description: Gun captains who learned their trade on Domain-era ballistic batteries and still trust nothing else. The older the ship, the better they shoot.

name: Tachyon Lens Technicians
description: Technicians who tune energy weapon optics by feel, trained on the most refined high-tech hulls they could get aboard. They do their best work on a ship that matches them.

name: Line Yard Ordnance Crew
description: An ordnance crew from the line yards that turn out midline warships by the hundred. They load missiles best on the kind of hull they grew up building.

name: Bulwark Riveters
description: Riveters who patch armor the old way, plate over plate. On a low-tech hull they never run out of places to add another layer.

name: Heritage Fire Control
description: The crew pieced this fire control suite together from generations of salvaged targeting cores. The more of the ship's lineage it recognizes, the further it reaches.

name: Mixed Doctrine Flight Instructors
description: Flight instructors who have taught pilots from every kind of fleet. They draw on whatever the ship's crew already knows to sharpen its pilots' aim.

name: Deck Armorers' Guild
description: Guild armorers who refit strikecraft with whatever plating the mothership's crew trusts most. The surer the crew, the tougher the craft.

name: Farige Blueprint Vault
description: A vault of Farige-pattern blueprints, every page annotated by Navarchy engineers who believed a ship should be built upon, never rebuilt. Each permanent refit the crew makes teaches them more of what the pages mean.

name: Absence of Light
description: A reactor shard pulled from a Stargazer wreck, burning with a light that casts no shadow. Around it the crew's old habits stop mattering, and every way of running the ship works as well as their best.

name: Bridge Officer
description: A career officer cleared to stand watch on a warship's bridge. A good one makes a crew quicker, steadier and harder to surprise.

name: Specialist Crew
description: Spacers with a trade worth keeping: riggers, medics, salvage hands. Give them proper quarters and they earn their berth twice over.

name: Drive Assembly
description: A rebuilt drive assembly with better injectors and a tuned thrust profile.

name: Reactor Regulator
description: A power regulation stack that sits between the reactor and everything that draws from it. Venting is faster and the weapons stop fighting the shields for every joule.

name: Fire Control Suite
description: Targeting computers, stabilised feeds and a gunnery officer who reads the solution aloud. Shells land where they were meant to, more often.

name: Shield Emitter
description: A recalibrated emitter array for the ship's shield generator. The bubble comes up faster, sits wider and costs less to hold.

name: Phase Coil Array
description: Replacement phase coils wound to a tighter tolerance than the originals. Slipping out of realspace takes less effort and the ship moves more freely while it is gone.

name: Deck Crew
description: A deck crew drilled on launch, recovery and rearm. Strikecraft spend less time on the deck and more time in the fight.

name: Armor Plate
description: Bolt-on plate cut from salvaged hull stock and fitted over the frame. It is heavy and it is ugly, and it keeps the crew alive.

name: Radiant Shield Lattice
description: Shield lattice cut from the prow of a dormant machine warship. It runs cold under fire that should melt it, and the crew have stopped asking why.

name: Equivalent Exchange Core
description: A reactor governor salvaged from a machine nexus, still balancing a ledger no human wrote. Whatever the ship gives up, it takes back in another form, and never as much as it was given.

name: Ordo Feed Conversion
description: Feed assemblies stripped from the warships of a machine ordo, made for weapons that never need reloading. The crew sealed the missile racks behind them and sent the ship's power where the ordnance used to go.

name: Displacer Failsafe
description: A displacer pulled from a machine frigate that kept slipping out of reach. Wired to the hull alarms, it throws the ship clear once, the moment the crew can no longer do it themselves.

name: Pather Wing Zealots
description: Pather pilots who swore their wings to the ship rather than to any machine mind. They fly as one congregation with the hull that launches them, and carry into battle whatever the crew have made of it.

name: Shard Microburn Cluster
description: Drive nodes pried from a shard found drifting far from any star. They burn without any fuel the crew can find, and the ship slips past other sensors the way the shard once did.

name: Tesseract Stillwell
description: Recovered from the heart of a tesseract wreck, it holds a pocket where time runs slow outside and fast within. The crew move quicker than they should around it, but their shots fade before reaching as far as they used to.

name: Reality Disruptor Echo
description: Fire-control salvaged alongside a reality disruptor from wreckage that should not exist. Now and then a shot leaves the barrel twice, and the crew have agreed not to ask which version of the ship fired the second.

name: Facet Mount Geometry
description: Mount rings cut from a facet hull, angled along lines the crew can't draw. Any small weapon seats in them, but each one draws more from the ship to stay there.
